gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-noto-sans-wan: Ethnocentric stretches its letters apart with a fast, aggressive stride, short ascenders perched over big bowls. Noto Sans Wancho follows in sans-serif form, hulking and chalky, with an e whose terminal gaps wide open.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-noto-traditio: Approachable and easygoing, Noto Traditional Nushu writes with a broad-nibbed stroke. Ethnocentric looms above it, fast and aggressive, while the sans-serif body fills each line with bowls that never curl shut, so a modest body size keeps things comfortable.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-numans: Wide, fast and a bit fierce, Ethnocentric spaces its smooth curves far apart. And Numans, a plain sans, matches that spacing with swollen, rope-tight lowercase and an s whose ends hang off the spine.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-onest: Ethnocentric hits fast and aggressive, with big bowls under short ascenders. Onest, a sans-serif with a gentle, single-weight line and no ink pooling in its turns, would look lost if the heading were shrunk small, since the lettering depends on size to dominate.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-orienta: Orienta is modern and neutral, its counters breathing open like a hollow reed and its cases barely differing in height. And Ethnocentric brings the sharp, fast, aggressive side, so this sans-serif feels like the quiet partner to a loud one.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-pathway-extre: Positive tracking pushes every Ethnocentric letter apart, giving the display face its fast, aggressive look. Pathway Extreme, sans-serif and stubby, sits beside it, big in x-height and open in its rounds, with heading use best kept large and short.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-pt-sans-capti: PT Sans Caption reads professional and contemporary, its bowls left unclosed and inviting. And over a longer stretch, those big-bodied lowercase letters stay friendly, while Ethnocentric above it keeps its fast, aggressive edge.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-ruda: Ethnocentric drives hard and fast, with short ascenders above big bowls and a smooth read. And Ruda, a wire-like sans-serif with wide-mouthed rounds, gives screen reading a sizable x-height, so body text can stay modest.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-saira: Neutral is the mood Saira brings, with a visible gap through each s and rounds that stretch toward the top line. Ethnocentric, by contrast, feels fast and aggressive, and Saira lets that spaced-out heading push forward while it stays put.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-sarpanch: Fast, aggressive and widely spaced, Ethnocentric hits like a shove. Sarpanch, a sans-serif with an open-mouthed e and a compact gap between x-height and ascender line, is the approachable counterweight that makes the pair work.
